title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident shows identity impersonation at scale, where artificial intelligence was used to create fake videos and social media profiles posing as a real attorney. The deployment failure was on social media platforms, where hundreds of fraudulent accounts operated across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram without being caught by platform moderation until an anti-piracy company intervened. The scam targeted vulnerable immigrants seeking legal services, directing them to make payments through digital apps to numbers not belonging to the impersonated attorney.

The failure to catch this before it caused harm was a breakdown in platform content moderation. No human review appears to have occurred at the point these profiles were created or when they began soliciting payments. The scammers used AI-generated video content to increase the volume and credibility of the impersonation beyond what manual fraud alone could achieve. It is not established who created the AI content, what platform moderation systems were in place, or why they failed to flag hundreds of profiles making identical claims.

What this shows is a vulnerability in how social media platforms verify identity claims and monitor for coordinated fraud. The impersonation was discovered only when people contacted the real attorney's office, meaning the system relied on victims to report the harm rather than preventing it. Catching this would have required either human review of new high-volume account creation or AI systems trained to detect coordinated impersonation patterns.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an extensive AI-driven fraud scheme. Scammers have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using artificial intelligence to impersonate him, offering immigration services he never provides. The fraudulent content appears on multiple platforms including TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, directing vulnerable immigrants to contact numbers via WhatsApp and requesting payments between $2,200 and other amounts through digital payment apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal first discovered the scheme when potential clients called his office, though suspicious activity began last October and escalated dramatically in recent months.

To combat the fraud, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms. The scams typically present fake testimonials from supposed former clients or claim to offer US residency assistance to undocumented immigrants. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the source of the scams. He is advising immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and to avoid paying for immigration services through direct payment apps or over the phone.
